title: Problem Details
description: Learn to use ProblemDetails for standardized error responses.

data.text: **ProblemDetails** is the standardized, machine-readable format ASP.NET Core uses to communicate HTTP error information. It is defined by **RFC 7807** (and extended by **RFC 9457**) and gives every client a predictable shape to parse instead of free-form error strings.

terms.definition: The original IETF specification that defines the Problem Details for HTTP APIs JSON format.
The 2023 successor to RFC 7807 that clarifies the format and adds minor extensions.
The .NET type that represents the RFC 7807 payload. It includes type, title, status, detail, and instance.
A subclass that adds an Errors dictionary mapping property names to error messages.
The media type clients use to identify ProblemDetails responses.

rows: A URL identifying the error type. Defaults to about:blank.
A short, human-readable summary of the problem.
A longer, human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence.
A unique identifier for this specific occurrence (often the request path).
The distributed trace id, when activity tracing is enabled.

data.caption: How validation failures become ProblemDetails responses.
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Client
  participant ApiController
  participant ModelBinder
  Client->>ApiController: POST /users (invalid JSON)
  ApiController->>ModelBinder: Bind and validate
  ModelBinder-->>ApiController: ModelState.IsValid = false
  ApiController-->>Client: 400 application/problem+json
  Client->>Client: Parse type/title/status/errors

data.text: When a controller is decorated with [ApiController] and model validation fails, ASP.NET Core emits a ValidationProblemDetails response automatically. You do not need to write any code to enable it.

data.title: Automatic 400 ValidationProblemDetails
data.content: The JSON body returned by ASP.NET Core when CreateUserRequest fails validation. The errors dictionary maps property names to arrays of messages.

data.title: Default Content-Type
data.text: ASP.NET Core serializes ProblemDetails with the content type application/problem+json. Clients can branch on this header to render error UIs differently from success payloads.

You can return ProblemDetails from any action by using the ControllerBase.Problem helper or by returning ValidationProblem. These helpers fill in sensible defaults and produce the correct content type.

data.title: Returning ProblemDetails Manually
data.content: Using ControllerBase.Problem to return a 404 with a stable type URL.

data.text: ASP.NET Core exposes AddProblemDetails() so you can configure how every ProblemDetails response is shaped. You can customize the default type URI, add extension members, and decide which status codes produce ProblemDetails.

data.title: Configuring ProblemDetails in Program.cs
data.content: Registering and customizing AddProblemDetails so 404 and 406 responses also return RFC 7807 payloads.

data.title: Register AddProblemDetails Once
data.text: AddProblemDetails() is enough on its own to enable ProblemDetails for client errors and exceptions when paired with UseExceptionHandler(). You do not need to call AddControllers().AddProblemDetails() separately.

cards.title: Customized ProblemDetails
pros: Includes correlation IDs and tenant info
Consistent across client and server errors
cons: Clients must know your type URIs

data.title: Add Custom ProblemDetails to a Sample API
data.description: Refactor an existing controller to return ProblemDetails for every error path.
steps: Add AddProblemDetails() to the DI container in Program.cs.
Add UseStatusCodePages() so empty 404 responses become ProblemDetails.
Replace every return NotFound() / return BadRequest() with Problem(...).
Add a custom extension that includes the correlation id.
Use curl or Postman to confirm the response uses application/problem+json.
data.expectedOutcome: Every error response in the API uses the same JSON envelope, with stable type URIs and a correlation id.

items.text: AddProblemDetails() is registered in the service container
Every action returns Problem(...) or ValidationProblem(...) for failures
Trace id is included as an extension field
Documented type URIs are stable across releases

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: ASP.NET Core emits them automatically for 400 responses with [ApiController]
Use AddProblemDetails() to customize extensions and defaults
Return Problem(...) or ValidationProblem(...) for consistent error shapes
Always include a trace id for debugging
data.takeaway: Standardized error payloads turn 'works on my machine' into 'works for every client.'
